prompt:
gen/build_reports.py reads an order export (default input/orders.csv) and writes report files into an output folder (default out/). On this Windows machine it produces wrong files, and it fails on some input. It writes four files today and must now write six (customers.csv and by_month.csv are new). Fix and extend the script so that `python gen/build_reports.py` (and with --input PATH and --out DIR) writes exactly the output described here. DIR may not exist yet (parent folders included), may already exist, and may contain spaces and non ASCII characters.

Input: input/orders.csv has the columns id, customer, amount, status and date (date is optional in other exports). It uses CRLF line endings and may start with a UTF-8 byte order mark. Another export may use LF, may have empty lines, and may have spaces around the id, customer and status values. The file is CSV as in RFC 4180: a quoted field can contain commas, doubled quotes ("") and line breaks. Empty lines are ignored and do not count as rows, and a quoted field that spans several lines is one row. Amounts can be written with thousands separators inside quotes ("1,250.00"), with no decimals (5), or with more than two decimals (2.675). No CR character may ever reach an output file.

Cleaning, for every row. Whitespace here means space, tab, CR and LF. id: trimmed. customer: trimmed, and every run of whitespace inside it becomes one space (so a name written over two lines is one line in every output). status: trimmed and lower cased ("PAID " becomes paid). amount: remove every comma, then it must be digits optionally followed by a dot and more digits (no sign, no currency symbol, no leading or trailing dot, no exponent), otherwise the row is invalid. A row with an empty id is skipped and written to stderr as `skipped row N: missing id`; otherwise a row with an invalid amount is skipped and written as `skipped row N: invalid amount`. N is the 1 based number of the row among the data rows (empty lines are not counted). Skipped rows are in no output file, and the exit code stays 0. date: only its first 7 characters YYYY-MM matter. A date written as YYYY-MM-DD with a month from 01 to 12 belongs to the month YYYY-MM (the day is not checked). A blank, missing or any other date belongs to the month `unknown`.

Output rules for all six files:
1. Every line ends with LF, never CRLF, on every platform.
2. Each file ends with exactly one newline: no missing newline and no empty last line.
3. Each file is UTF-8 without a BOM, and non ASCII characters are written as they are (also in the JSON file, never as \uXXXX escapes).
4. Orders are sorted by the number after the last hyphen of the id, as a number (A-9 before A-10 before A-100), and then by the whole id. An id with no hyphen, or whose text after the last hyphen is not only the digits 0 to 9, has the number 0.
5. Amounts are parsed as decimal numbers from the text, rounded half up to two decimals, and always printed with a dot and exactly two decimals (5 becomes 5.00, 2.675 becomes 2.68). Totals are the sum of the rounded amounts.
6. Orders whose status is cancelled are left out of summary.txt, by_customer.json, report.md, customers.csv and by_month.csv, but they stay in orders.tsv.
7. Orders whose status is refunded stay in all of those files, but their amount counts as negative in every total (summary.txt total, each customer total, the report total and each month total). In report.md a refunded amount is printed with a minus sign, for example -19.90 (a refunded amount of 0.00 is printed 0.00). In orders.tsv the amount stays as written in the input. A refunded order counts in the order counts and the customer count, but it is never the largest order.
8. customers.csv has the header `customer,orders,total` and one row per customer with the same order count and total as by_customer.json, sorted by total (as a number, largest first) and then by customer name in code point order. Fields are quoted the way a CSV writer does it: only when they contain a comma, a double quote or a line break, with quotes doubled.
9. by_month.csv has the header `month,orders,total` and one row per month with the order count and total of the orders that count, sorted by month, followed by the row for `unknown` last when there is one.
10. When no order qualifies as the largest, the line in summary.txt is `largest: none`. A file with no orders still has its header or its fixed lines: summary.txt reads `orders: 0`, `customers: 0`, `total: 0.00`, `largest: none`; by_customer.json is `{}`; report.md has the heading, the table header, a blank line and `Total: 0.00`.
11. In summary.txt, orders is the number of orders that count, customers is the number of different customer names among them, total is their total, and largest is the id and the amount (two decimals) of the order with the highest amount among the orders that are neither cancelled nor refunded. On a tie the order that comes first in the order of rule 4 wins. The four lines are `orders: N`, `customers: N`, `total: X` and `largest: ID (X)`.

Exit codes and messages: when the input file cannot be read or is not valid UTF-8 the script writes `error: cannot read <the path as given>` to stderr, exits with code 2 and creates no output folder. Otherwise it exits with code 0 and its stdout is the single line `wrote 6 files to <the out folder as given>` (UTF-8, ending in LF, also when the folder name has non ASCII characters and stdout is a pipe).

For the supplied input/orders.csv the six files must be byte for byte these (\t is a tab character):

summary.txt
```
orders: 5
customers: 3
total: 1623.15
largest: A-9 (1250.00)
```

```
A-10\tŁukasz Nowak\t310.50\tpaid
A-11\tAlan Wu\t0.75\tshipped
A-12\tZoë Martin\t19.90\tpaid
A-100\tŁukasz Nowak\t42.00\tpaid
A-101\tZoë Martin\t5.00\tcancelled
```

```
  },
```
